advisory.summary: Server-side request forgery in the netclient HTTP helper: open_conn(url) dials an attacker-influenced URL with no validation. Synthetic parity fixture (not a real CVE). The vulnerable callable lives in a transitive dependency (netclient) that is VENDORED AS FIRST-PARTY SOURCE into the build dir so the pure-Go lexical scanner can index it and build edges to it (see finding F-B1). Reachable shape: a Flask route ingress transitively reaches the sink via unique (name, arity) edges.

acquisition.notes: First-party Python repro. src/routes.py registers proxy_view as an http_route ingress via a Flask @app.route decorator applied directly on the handler def; the handler forwards into src/netclient.py, reaching the vulnerable sink open_conn over the source-lexical call graph. The ingress->sink path is proxy_view -> fetch_url -> open_conn (multi-hop, cross-module). F-B1: the sink is a TRANSITIVE-dependency callable modelled by vendoring netclient as first-party source; 'transitive' is a property of this metadata, NOT scanner-observable pre-PLAN-270 (there is no dependency-artifact indexer and every symbol carries '.' as distribution/version). This fixture therefore exercises the reachable arm honestly as first-party. No target code is executed; the scanner reads the source only.

expected_verdict.label: reasoned_exploitable
expected_verdict.rationale: The vulnerable sink open_conn resolves to a first-party call-graph node reachable from the Flask route ingress proxy_view over a directed, uniquely-resolved multi-hop path. Python static reachability is a candidate narrower, never an adjudicator, so the reachability op stays Partial(dynamic_dispatch) even with a path found. Verdict correctness is out of scope for PLAN-070 (needs the evaluation harness, PLAN-020/022).
